title: Start Smaller Than You Think
pin_title: ADHD Starting Tip: Make the First Step Almost Too Small
description: The first step often feels too big, so shrink it until it almost feels silly. Open the notebook. Write one word. Fill one glass of water. Tiny starts knock the resistance down and tell your brain it is safe to begin. You can always do more once you have started. #ADHD #ADHDTips #SmallSteps

title: Ride the Energy Wave
pin_title: ADHD Energy: Work With the Waves Not Against Them
description: ADHD energy comes in waves instead of a steady stream. Notice when a small spark appears and ride it for a few minutes, then rest without guilt. Fighting the low tide wastes more energy than it saves. A short burst still counts as progress. #ADHD #ADHDLife #EnergyManagement

title: Listen to the Body First
pin_title: ADHD Body Signals: Hunger and Thirst Look Like Laziness
description: Sometimes what feels like cannot focus is simply a hungry or thirsty body. Drink a glass of water or eat a small snack before you decide you are stuck. Your brain works better when the basics are covered. Kindness to the body is not procrastination. #ADHD #ADHDTips #SelfCare

title: Pause Is Allowed
pin_title: ADHD Pause: Stopping Is Not the Same as Quitting
description: You are allowed to stop in the middle and come back later. A pause is not failure, it is part of how many ADHD brains work. Leave a tiny note about the next step so future you can restart easily. The path stays open even when you rest. #ADHD #SelfCompassion #ADHDTips
scene_prompt: A soft wooden bench under a gentle glowing tree with one tiny paper note left on the seat, {mascot} walking away calmly, warm afternoon light

title: Keep One Thing Visible
pin_title: ADHD Focus Tip: Hide the Extra Choices
description: Too many open options make starting harder. Keep only the one thing you need right now in sight and put the rest away or in a later list. Fewer visible choices calm the brain and make the next step clearer. You can always bring the others back. #ADHD #FocusHacks #ADHDTips

title: Press Restart Kindly
pin_title: ADHD Restart: Begin Again Without the Story
description: Missed yesterday? That does not write a story about today. Press a kind restart: open the page, write one sentence, or set a gentle five-minute timer. Every morning is allowed to be a fresh start. You do not have to catch up first. #ADHD #ADHDTips #FreshStart

title: A Timer That Does Not Shout
pin_title: ADHD Timer Tip: Soft Countdowns Work Better
description: Loud countdown timers can increase anxiety. Try a soft visual timer or a gentle song length instead. The goal is a friendly boundary, not pressure. Pair it with one tiny task and stop when it ends without guilt. Small time boxes keep the day kinder. #ADHD #FocusHacks #ADHDTips

title: Notice the Tiny Wins
pin_title: ADHD Wins: Celebrate the Small Steps Out Loud
description: Finishing a big task is not the only win. Opening the document, writing one line, or putting one item away all count. Say the win out loud or write it down. Noticing progress teaches your brain that effort is safe and worthwhile. Tiny still matters. #ADHD #ADHDTips #SmallWins
